## Source-backed inputs (dependency C66-GEO-Z)

ATT-0065, independently confirmed by REV-0108 and REV-0109, is the sole load-bearing geometric dependency. The following claims are used by explicit artifact ID and are not re-derived here beyond the arithmetic specializations needed for ranks and minors:

- CLM-0065-5: fibrewise O(4)+O(5) supplies a canonical filtration 0->W_4->W->W_5->0 with deg W_4=20 and deg W_5=16 at g=6, without a global splitting of F or of W.
- CLM-0065-1: under the degree inequalities, pi_*W and pi_*(W|Gamma) are locally free with arbitrary base change, and Fit_0(coker phi)=I_{2n}(phi).
- CLM-0065-3: with d_4-n>2g-2, the filtered snake lemma gives coker(phi) isomorphic to coker(phi_5) with no global splitting.
- CLM-0065-2 and CLM-0065-4: Fit_0(coker Phi)=I_e on Pic^0, hence Fit_0(coker phi)=a_N^*I_e scheme-theoretically over possibly nonreduced locally Noetherian bases, with smooth-atlas descent.
- CLM-0065-7 through CLM-0065-9: ambient comparison only under the explicit CE resolution and q_*script-W freeness/base-change hypotheses; fibrewise balancedness kills R^1 s_* End(F).

Packet findings FND-0097 and FND-0099 corroborate that the filtration (not a global split) and the two degree vanishings deg W_4=20>10, deg W_4(-Gamma)=14>10 are the correct hypotheses for the filtered Fitting reduction. SRC-0004 is used only through ATT-0065 for the CE sign convention and deg(W_f)=4g+12-4f.

Primary working-context constraints respected throughout: no global split from fibrewise balancedness; no scheme-theoretic ideal equality from geometric points alone (Fitting comparison is routed through ATT-0065); no image dimension from source count 15+2=17; no reduced-support nonemptiness from chi(L)=1; no Proj(pi_*L) identification when h^0 jumps; no lci conclusion from expected-versus-actual codimension; no W_5 isomorphic to omega^2(-D) elevation.

## Proved step 1: ranks and base change

[proved from degree arithmetic + dependency CLM-0065-1/5]

At g=6 one has deg W_4=20 and deg W_5=16, both strictly larger than 2g-2=10. Fibrewise Serre duality kills H^1(W_f), so R^1 pi_* W_f=0. Riemann-Roch gives ranks h^0(W_4)=20-6+1=15 and h^0(W_5)=16-6+1=11. Because Gamma is the disjoint union of six sections, each pi_*(W_f|_Gamma) is locally free of rank 6. The filtration and exactness of pi_* along 0->W_4->W->W_5->0 (which uses R^1 pi_* W_4=0) give rank(pi_*W)=26 and rank(pi_*(W|_Gamma))=12. Thus phi has ranks 26->12. Local freeness and arbitrary locally Noetherian base change are supplied by CLM-0065-1 together with the degree vanishings. Fit_0(coker phi)=I_12(phi) as the ideal of maximal minors of a map into a free rank-12 sheaf.

## Proved step 2: global maximal-minor identity without splitting

[proved; repairs ATT-0067]

Also deg W_4(-Gamma)=20-6=14>10, so R^1 pi_* W_4(-Gamma)=0 and phi_4 is surjective (equivalently coker(phi_4)=0). Applying the snake lemma to the two exact evaluation rows for the filtered sequence yields the canonical dependency-backed isomorphism coker(phi) isomorphic to coker(phi_5) (CLM-0065-3; FND-0097/0099). Zeroth Fitting ideals depend only on the cokernel. Since phi and phi_5 are locally free presentations with free targets of ranks 12 and 6,

Fit_0(coker phi)=I_12(phi)=Fit_0(coker phi_5)=I_6(phi_5)

as ideal sheaves on all of B. This is a global identity; it does not use a block-diagonal minor factorization and does not require W to split. (ATT-0067 reached I_12=I_6(phi_5) only on splitting opens by a column-selection product, which REV-0112 correctly rejected as a global claim.)

By CLM-0065-2 and CLM-0065-4 the common ideal equals a_N^*I_e, represents relative triviality of N, commutes with arbitrary locally Noetherian base change, and descends along smooth atlases. This is a pure pass-through of the dual-confirmed nonreduced Fitting/Picard comparison; fibrewise deg-0 triviality alone would be FND-0046-insufficient and is not used as a substitute.

## Proved step 3: submaximal minors I_11(phi)=O_B

[proved; completes the Fitting frontier package]

Fix a geometric point b of B. From the evaluation sequence for W_{5,b} and H^1(W_{5,b})=0 one has coker(phi_{5,b}) isomorphic to H^1(C_b,W_{5,b}(-Gamma_b)). Serre duality identifies its dual with H^0(C_b,N_b), where N_b=omega_{C_b} tensor W_{5,b}^vee(Gamma_b) has degree 10-16+6=0. A degree-zero line bundle on a smooth projective connected curve has either no nonzero section or is trivial with a one-dimensional space of sections. Hence dim coker(phi_b)=dim coker(phi_{5,b}) is either 0 or 1, so rank(phi_b) is always at least 11. Every geometric point of B therefore lies in an open on which some 11-by-11 minor is a unit. On a locally Noetherian scheme, an ideal sheaf whose vanishing locus is empty on all geometric points is the unit ideal. Thus I_11(phi)=O_B as ideal sheaves. Equivalently, phi has rank exactly 12 off the failure locus and exactly 11 on it; the degeneracy is pure corank one.

(The same corank bound shows that the expected Porteous codimension of {rk phi_5 <=5} for ranks 11->6 is (11-5)(6-5)=6, matching dim Pic^0=g=6 for the section a_N^{-1}(e). This is recorded as bookkeeping only; no lci, depth, or image claim is drawn from expected-versus-actual comparisons.)

## Proved step 4: geometric rank-drop fibre and dimension formula

[proved]

For an effective degree-six divisor Delta on a geometric fibre C_b, the same degree-zero calculation gives rank drop of the W_5 evaluation exactly when H^0(omega tensor W_5^vee(Delta)) is nonzero, equivalently when that degree-zero line bundle is trivial, equivalently O(Delta) isomorphic to L_b=W_{5,b} tensor omega^{-1}. Thus the geometric rank-drop set among all effective degree-six divisors is the complete linear system |L_b|. The full Abel-Jacobi fibre is the projective space of nonzero sections of L_b modulo scalars, so its dimension is h^0(L_b)-1. (Relative Abel-Jacobi model: FND-0107; no global Proj(pi_*L) is asserted where h^0 may jump.)

## Proved step 5: unconditional h^0 range and hyperelliptic equality case

[proved; aligns with FND-0073 and FND-0103]

Since deg L_b=16-10=6, Riemann-Roch gives chi(L_b)=1. With M_b=omega^2 tensor W_{5,b}^vee=omega tensor L_b^{-1}, Serre duality gives h^1(L_b)=h^0(M_b), hence h^0(L_b)=1+h^0(M_b)>=1 and deg M_b=4. No identification W_5 isomorphic to omega^2(-D) is used (GAP-Z-W5D avoided).

If h^0(M_b)=0 then h^0(L_b)=1. If h^0(M_b)>=1 then h^1(M_b)=h^0(L_b)=1+h^0(M_b)>=2, so M_b is special and Clifford's theorem supplies h^0(M_b)-1 <= deg(M_b)/2=2, i.e. h^0(M_b)<=3. Therefore 1<=h^0(L_b)<=4 and dim|L_b| lies in {0,1,2,3}. In particular the stratum h^0(L)=5 is empty.

For equality h^0(M_b)=3: |M_b| is a g^2_4. It is base-point-free, because a base point would leave a degree-at-most-3 line bundle with three sections, contradicting Clifford. The induced nondegenerate map C_b->P^2 has degree times image degree equal to four. It cannot be birational onto a plane quartic, because the geometric genus of a plane quartic is at most three. The image cannot be a line (which would give h^0<=2). Hence the map is a double cover of a smooth conic, so C_b is hyperelliptic and M_b isomorphic to twice its g^1_2. Conversely, on a hyperelliptic curve one has h^0(2 g^1_2)=3, giving h^0(L_b)=4. Thus h^0(L_b)=4 if and only if C_b is hyperelliptic and M_b isomorphic to 2 g^1_2. Whether such fibres meet the balanced locus, and whether h^0(L)=3 constantly on the balanced locus, remain open.

## Proved step 6: reduced-support scope

[proved caveat; FND-0064, FND-0083]

The locus of six pairwise-distinct support points is open in |L_b| (complement of the image of the big diagonal). Ordering it is a finite etale S_6-torsor at stack level of pairwise-distinct sections (FND-0064); freeness can fail on coarse moduli and is not claimed there. Therefore the ordered reduced-support fibre is either empty or has dimension h^0(L_b)-1. Riemann-Roch proves nonemptiness only of the full |L_b|; chi(L)=1 does not force a reduced member (e.g. 6p may be the unique effective divisor). This respects the primary and extended constraints against concluding reduced-support/Conf_6 nonemptiness from chi(L)=1 alone.

## Ambient comparison (source-backed, conditional)

Under the explicit ambient hypotheses of ATT-0065 (standard degree-four CE resolution of I_C and finite local freeness/base-change of q_* script-W), CLM-0065-7 through CLM-0065-9 give that the ambient evaluation has the same cokernel and Fitting ideal as the intrinsic map once R^1 s_* End(F)=0, which fibrewise balancedness supplies. Fibrewise balancedness alone does not discharge the equation-bundle freeness hypothesis (REV-0108 FC-AMBIENT-EQN-BUNDLE-REMAINS-HYP); that hypothesis is retained.

## Computational hypotheses and blocked routes

No finite experiment or computational hypothesis is used to close any universal claim. SHA-pinned arithmetic (deg W_f, obstruction degrees -4/0, chi(L)=1, deg M=4, expected codimension 6, source count 15+(h^0-1)) motivates bookkeeping only.

None of the four blocked routes is used: the argument is a fibre-level determinantal/linear-series computation and uses no vcd vanishing, undecorated graph complex, point counts, or forgetful local-system renaming.

## Gaps (explicitly undischarged)

GAP-REDUCED-SUPPORT: nonemptiness of the reduced-support open and ordered Conf_6 incidence on every balanced geometric fibre.
GAP-H0-CONSTANCY: constancy of h^0(L) (equivalently exclusion of values 1,2 and of hyperelliptic balanced members) on the balanced locus.
GAP-Z-W5D: no identification W_5 isomorphic to omega^2(-D) or L isomorphic to omega(-D) is asserted.
GAP-IMAGE: balanced-base dimension, image dimension, numerical codimension, generic finiteness, components, stabilizers, closure, and local lci/Gysin structure in M_{6,6}.
GAP-AMBIENT-BUNDLE: ambient comparison retains ATT-0065's equation-bundle freeness/base-change hypothesis.
GAP-RED-0001: no purity, Tate type, vanishing, or resolution of the global target.

theorem_statement: Theorem (filtered balanced CE rank-drop ideals and fibre dimensions at (g,n)=(6,6)). Let k be a characteristic-zero field and B a locally Noetherian k-scheme. Let pi:C->B be smooth proper with geometrically connected genus-six fibres, and let Gamma be the union of six pairwise-disjoint sections of pi. Assume balanced tetragonal Casnati-Ekedahl data supply the canonical filtration 0->W_4->W->W_5->0 on C with W_4,W_5 invertible of constant fibre degrees 20 and 16 (no global splitting of W required). Write phi:pi_*W->pi_*(W|_Gamma) and phi_f:pi_*W_f->pi_*(W_f|_Gamma) for the evaluation maps, L:=W_5 tensor omega_{C/B}^{-1}, N:=omega_{C/B} tensor W_5^vee(Gamma), a_N:B->Pic^0_{C/B} the classifying map of N, and e the identity section of Pic^0. Then: (i) pi_*W_4, pi_*W_5, pi_*W, pi_*(W_4|_Gamma), pi_*(W_5|_Gamma), and pi_*(W|_Gamma) are locally free of ranks 15, 11, 26, 6, 6, and 12 respectively, and formation of these sheaves and of phi, phi_f commutes with arbitrary locally Noetherian base change. (ii) Without any global splitting of W one has a canonical isomorphism coker(phi) isomorphic to coker(phi_5), hence Fit_0(coker phi)=I_12(phi)=I_6(phi_5) as ideal sheaves on B. (iii) Moreover I_11(phi)=O_B: every geometric fibre of phi has rank 12 or 11 and never smaller. Combined with the dual-confirmed Fitting/Picard identity of ATT-0065, the common maximal-minor ideal equals a_N^*I_e scheme-theoretically, represents relative triviality of N, and descends along smooth atlases. (iv) Under the additional ambient CE resolution and equation-bundle finite-local-freeness/base-change hypotheses of ATT-0065, the ambient CE evaluation map has the same cokernel and the same failure scheme. (v) On every geometric fibre C_b the geometric rank-drop set among effective degree-six divisors is the complete linear system |L_b|, of dimension h^0(L_b)-1. Writing M_b:=omega_{C_b}^{tensor 2} tensor W_{5,b}^vee one has deg M_b=4 and h^0(L_b)=1+h^0(M_b), so 1<=h^0(L_b)<=4 and dim|L_b| lies in {0,1,2,3}. Equality h^0(L_b)=4 holds if and only if C_b is hyperelliptic and M_b isomorphic to 2 g^1_2. (vi) The ordered reduced-support fibre is an open finite etale S_6-cover (at stack level) of the reduced-support open in |L_b|; it is either empty or of dimension h^0(L_b)-1. Nonemptiness of that open is not implied by chi(L_b)=1.
